reportSubtitle: Text intake summary based on patient-reported concerns
executiveSummary: The intake describes a patient in the context of a highly conflictual divorce, reporting distress related to alleged false accusations, prolonged separation from children, and ongoing emotional, relational, and behavioral concerns. He reports past passive thoughts of not wanting to live during the initial crisis, but also states he is not the suicidal type and says he has since engaged in extensive healing. He identifies ongoing needs around pornography relapse prevention, sexual boundaries, emotional regulation, insight and accountability, parenting and reintegration with children, communication and conflict management, self-esteem, trust, and social withdrawal. Faith is explicitly part of his coping, alongside support from Mr Louw Alberts.
sessionSummary:
The patient wrote that he is in the middle of an extremely messy divorce and says his ex falsely accused him of abuse, molestation, and other serious allegations. He reports that two psychological forensic investigations, a police forensic investigation, and a social worker forensic investigation with the children all confirmed his innocence, according to him. He described being deeply broken and traumatized when the situation began and said that in the beginning he did not want to live anymore, though he clarified that he is not the suicidal type and would have welcomed death rather than actively wanting to die. He said he has gone through extensive healing since then, but still misses his family and is still fighting to see his children after one and a half years. He stated the children are in therapy to prepare for reintegration.

He then listed the areas he believes he still needs help with. These included pornography relapse prevention; healthy sexual boundaries, especially in light of past experimentation with his ex and a third partner; emotional regulation for stress, sorrow, anger, rejection, and loneliness; insight and accountability regarding his actions and relationship dynamics; parenting capacity and child-focused contact for rebuilding a relationship with the children; communication and conflict management for co-parenting; self-esteem, social withdrawal, dependency, and trust; and reintegration therapy for when he sees the children again. He said he feels regret and self-hate about what he allowed in the marriage, believes he should have rejected those behaviors, and acknowledges that he used to internalize everything and take the blame. He said he discusses these matters regularly with his mother. He also said he does not hate his ex, feels sorry for her, and regrets his share of her pain. He expressed that he is excited but also scared about seeing his children again, and he wants guidance on how to speak to them without making their mother seem like the bad guy.

riskFormulation.riskLevel: Low to moderate, based on transcript only
riskFormulation.summary: The transcript contains a historical statement of passive death wishes at the start of the divorce crisis, but the patient denies being suicidal and does not describe current intent, plan, or self-harm behavior. Current risk concerns are more strongly centered on shame, loneliness, grief, trust injury, and ongoing divorce/parenting stress. Because the report is text-based and no direct risk interview is documented, current risk should be clarified in follow-up.

reviewerConsiderations: The intake metadata lists the patient name as Harry, while the transcript names Eugene Mulder; per instructions, use the intake data patient name exactly.
The transcript contains patient-reported claims about forensic investigations and innocence; these are not independently corroborated in the supplied data.
The transcript includes a historical passive death wish but no current suicide assessment; follow-up risk screening is indicated.
Gender is not specified in intake metadata; avoid gendered pronouns in any narrative not directly quoted.
The report should be interpreted as a text intake summary rather than a full clinical interview.
facilitatorSummary: This intake centers on divorce-related trauma, prolonged separation from children, and the patient’s wish for help with relapse prevention, sexual boundaries, emotional regulation, self-blame, parenting reintegration, and co-parenting communication. He reports past passive death wishes during the initial crisis but denies being suicidal. He also identifies faith, his mother, and prior support from Mr Louw Alberts as important resources. Follow-up should clarify current safety, current symptoms, and the practical/legal context for child contact and reintegration.
clinicalWorkingNotes: Patient presents as reflective, motivated, and highly focused on repair and prevention. The narrative is organized around loss, shame, and a desire to be safe and child-focused. The most clinically salient issues from the transcript are: historical passive death wish during acute divorce stress; ongoing grief/loneliness; self-critical shame; trust injury; and treatment goals around pornography relapse prevention, sexual boundaries, and parenting reintegration. No diagnosis is made here. No current active suicidal intent is documented in the transcript. Use caution not to overstate corroboration of legal or forensic claims.
